executive_summary: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 revenue reached $215.938 billion, up 65% year over year, with Data Center revenue at $193.737 billion, up 68%. GAAP net income rose 65% to $120.067 billion. The growth engine remained AI infrastructure, while GAAP gross margin fell 3.9 points to 71.1% as the business shifted to Blackwell full scale data center solutions and absorbed a $4.5 billion H20 charge.

insights.title: Data Center carried the year
insights.text: Data Center revenue was $193.737B, about 89.7% of total FY2026 revenue, and grew 68% year over year. NVIDIA says accelerated computing and AI drove the increase.

insights.title: Earnings scaled faster than operating income
insights.text: GAAP net income rose 65% and operating income rose 60%, even as gross margin declined 3.9 points. The 10-K attributes the margin decline to the transition from Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full scale data center solutions and the H20 charge.

insights.title: China and customer concentration remain watch items
insights.text: The 10-K says one direct customer represented 22% of FY2026 revenue and another 14%, primarily in Compute & Networking. It also says NVIDIA was effectively foreclosed from China's data center compute market at fiscal year end; Q1 FY2027 guidance assumes no China Data Center compute revenue.

watch_items: Gross margin: 71.1% GAAP in FY2026 versus 75.0% in FY2025.
Product transition: Blackwell full scale data center solutions and a faster annual architecture cadence can create supply, qualification and timing volatility.
China/export controls: the company reported effective foreclosure from China's data center compute market at FY2026 year end and no China Data Center compute revenue in Q1 FY2027 outlook.
Non-GAAP comparability: beginning in Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA will include stock based compensation expense in non-GAAP measures.
